title: Pearl Harbor: The Fuel Tanks Japan Left Standing

scenes.text: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor for oil... then left four and a half million barrels of American fuel untouched.
In 1941, an American oil embargo threatened Japan's war in China.
Japan's leaders chose to seize oil fields in the Dutch East Indies, today's Indonesia.
But the American Pacific Fleet could threaten that advance.
So Japan struck Hawaii, hoping to cripple the fleet and buy time for its conquests.
On December seventh, Japanese aircraft devastated American battleships.
Yet the fuel tanks and repair yards largely survived. The American carriers were also absent.
Those surviving resources helped the Pacific Fleet keep fighting.
Japan hit the ships, but left America the fuel to fight a long war.
